key_insight: Two-way coupling between superfluid vortices and normal-fluid turbulence actively rolls quantized vortices into coherent bundles, reproducing a classical-like multiscale hierarchy and a Kolmogorov energy cascade.
engineering_relevance: The result clarifies how heat transfer, dissipation, and vortex organization in superfluid helium can be predicted and potentially controlled by accounting for mutual friction and two-fluid coupling.
method: Fully coupled vortex filament and Navier–Stokes simulations
Spatially periodic normal-fluid turbulence with mutual friction feedback
Comparison of vortex structure, spectra, and time scales across temperatures
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct simulation evidence of bundle formation, a k^-5/3 spectrum, and a coupling-time-to-dissipation-time threshold t_cl/τ_eta < 20 associated with stable bundles.
watch_item: The mechanism is demonstrated in a periodic simulation setting, so real-flow geometry, forcing details, and parameter ranges may limit immediate transferability.
paper_title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
